question: Summarize the company’s scale and fee economics and identify anything questionable.
answer: Assets under management were reported as $146.1 billion at 31 December 2025 and $142 billion at the fiscal year end of 31 March 2026; the memo explicitly treats these as different reporting dates rather than a discrepancy. These are date variants, not a conflict. Assets under advisement were $905 billion at 31 March 2026, and the firm described its combined asset footprint as about $1 trillion. Fee-earning AUM ended the fiscal year at $82 billion, while specialized funds were $41 billion and the evergreen platform was above $17.5 billion. The blended fee rate was 67 basis points and was said to be drifting up as the mix shifted toward specialized funds. For the fiscal year, management and advisory fees were $584.2 million, total fee-related revenue was $687 million, and fee-related earnings were $345 million with a 50 percent FRE margin. The memo identifies $8.2 billion of fee-earning AUM in a February-call note as incompatible with the $82 billion fiscal-year figure and does not resolve the source error. The verified sources contain a conflict. The disclosed fee mix percentages are only as of 31 December 2025 on a nine-month basis and should not be represented as fiscal-year figures. Year-over-year retroactive fees fell from nearly $21 million to about $3 million, which the memo warns can make quarterly growth look worse than underlying business growth.
